clue.text: Gloomy lines in part

indicators.note: in tells us the railway lines go inside the word for a portion

parts.note: part of something is some of it
BR, British Rail(ways), stands for railway lines

explanation.surface: Somebody remarks on the gloomy lines spoken in some part of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like dialogue in a theatrical part, but it is BR, British Railways, set inside SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a dark, dismal, cheerless mood.

clue.text: Did Runyon write more than this? Rather!

definitions.text: Did Runyon write more than this?
definitions.meaning: Damon Runyon's Broadway characters habitually say 'more than ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to a moderate degree, and Runyon's gangsters say 'more than' it constantly.

clue.text: Girls sees priest in Mass perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us the priest goes inside the rearranged word
perhaps means the word may appear in another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A girl spots a priest celebrating Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges MASS to MSSA, and 'in' puts ELI, the Biblical priest, after its M; 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a woman's name, from the Greek for honey bee.

clue.text: Barker embarrassed, having: given wrong clue?

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
a setter is one who sets puzzles, who would blush at having set a faulty clue

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler blushes after getting a clue wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a blushing puzzle compiler; the whole is a dog, a barker.
explanation.definitionFit: A red setter, an Irish setter, is a gun dog, and dogs bark.

clue.text: Gives secluded building to ladies

indicators.note: building means putting something together, so the letters of these words are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a remote, out-of-the-way building to a group of ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like a noun for a house, but it is the anagram signal working on TO LADIES; 'Gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secluded is cut off and set apart from others.

clue.text: Show's opening-Comedy Theatre ? What a shambles!

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a comedy theatre is a house full of laughter

explanation.surface: A critic sees a show open at the Comedy Theatre and pronounces it a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The Comedy Theatre is a real London theatre, but here it becomes a 'laughter house'. A shambles was originally a meat market, so it is fair for an abattoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambles once meant a butchers' market and so a place where animals are killed.

clue.text: Mistress fails to finish the racing circuit

indicators.note: fails to finish means the name loses its last letter, like a car retiring before the end

parts.note: Le Mans in France hosts the famous 24-hour motor race

explanation.surface: A mistress drops out of a motor race before the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fails to finish' cuts the S from LE MANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A leman is an archaic word for a lover or illicit sweetheart.

clue.text: Notes in peculiar strain

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so these letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Musical notes in an odd melody, a strain in the musical sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks musical next to 'Notes', but it means stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is the stress or strain felt under pressure.

clue.text: Insist on theologian holding up call

indicators.note: holding means the theologian's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: DD is a Doctor of Divinity

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a theologian delays a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses NAME to EMAN, and 'holding' places it inside DD, Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on something is to require it firmly.

clue.text: Prohibitionist chief has row — topping the news

parts.note: one who bans things is a banner
a head is a chief
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A temperance leader's quarrel makes the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line; 'Prohibitionist' suggests US Prohibition, but it is simply one who bans.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline in large type across the page tops the day's news.

clue.text: Play unfinished tune to arty people

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for a tune loses its final letter

parts.note: a tune is a melody
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate in the arts

explanation.surface: A half-written tune is offered to a bunch of arty types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts the last letter from MELODY to give MELOD; the two arty people are an RA (Royal Academician) and an MA (Master of Arts).
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage piece with exaggerated emotion.

clue.text: Note car number

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone jots down a car's registration number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a verb meaning jot down; it is a musical note, a half-note in American terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth two crotchets.

clue.text: Literary squire filmed

definitions.meaning: Squire ... is the hearty country landowner in Fielding's novel Tom Jones
a cowboy film is a genre picture of the American frontier, something filmed

explanation.definitionFit: Fielding's squire bears this surname, and the word also names a cowboy movie.

clue.text: A sort of violet or other flower

definitions.meaning: ... violet is a purple dye used as an antiseptic
a blue alpine bloom of the mountains

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an antiseptic purple dye and a blue mountain plant.

clue.text: Girl exercises to get fit

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT is physical training, gym exercises

explanation.surface: A girl works out to get into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' seems to mean healthy, but it is a verb: to make suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify it so that it suits a purpose.

clue.text: Strikingly good-—or just sound ?

explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for very fine and also a clattering noise.

clue.text: Member seen by somebody drawing a joker

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
one who draws or tugs is a puller

explanation.surface: A club member is spotted by someone sketching a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' looks like sketching, but it means pulling; 'seen by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who teases people with tall stories is a hoaxer and prankster.

clue.text: Shares in this robe ?

parts.note: shares are a financial stake; split the word for that stake after its first two letters and the rest is a church garment

explanation.surface: A question about owning shares in a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: Shares are an investment, which read as 'in' plus the rest gives a priest's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial garment worn by clergy.

clue.text: Applause, if deafening, would defeat its purpose

definitions.text: Applause, if deafening, would defeat its purpose

parts.words: Applause, if deafening, would defeat its purpose
parts.note: a cry of approval in Parliament that urges others to listen; if everyone were deaf it would be pointless

explanation.surface: A remark that thunderous clapping is self-defeating.
explanation.walkthrough: The parliamentary cheer literally tells people to listen, so deafening approval would undo it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British parliamentary cry of agreement voices approval of a speaker.

clue.text: Painfully repulsive spectacle ?

parts.note: an ugly sight is one that makes your vision organs hurt

explanation.surface: Something so hideous it hurts to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the term means aching eyes, which an ugly sight might cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an unsightly building or object.

clue.text: Author makes attempt to get letter written returned

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: returned means the spelt-out letter is turned back to front

parts.note: ESS is the letter S written out as a word

explanation.surface: A writer tries to get a letter he wrote sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reverses ESS, the letter S spelt out, to give SSE after GO. Edmund Gosse was a Victorian critic and author.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Gosse wrote Father and Son and much literary criticism.

clue.text: " Ambition should be made of stuff " (J. Caesar)

definitions.text: Ambition should be made of stuff

parts.words: Ambition should be made of stuff
parts.note: Antony's funeral speech in Julius Caesar says ambition should be made of more severe stuff; the missing word fills the gap

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows a dash between 'of' and 'stuff'. Antony says: 'Ambition should be made of sterner stuff'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the comparative of severe, harsh, strict.

clue.text: A supply of food on the vessel

parts.note: board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A cargo of food is loaded onto the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Board means daily meals, as in 'full board'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: As fortunate as Rossetti's damozel

definitions.meaning: Dante Gabriel Rossetti's poem and painting of a maiden in heaven

explanation.definitionFit: The word means lucky or holy, and titles Rossetti's poem of the heavenly maiden.

clue.text: Measures taken in advance

definitions.meaning: actions taken to deal with something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means precautionary actions and also paces made in going forward.

clue.text: Pound note up makes us ,uncommonly wealthy

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L stands for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone says that a pound note going up in value makes us unusually rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' looks like 'very', but it shuffles L (pound) with NOTE UP; 'makes us' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes lavish riches and luxurious abundance.

clue.text: Home for a �across the columns with key

annotationWithheld.why: Home for a serviceman, with key (scan): AB (serviceman) and E (key) leave OD unexplained, and no reading gives every letter
annotationWithheld.clue: Home for a �across the columns with key

clue.text: Rudeness of officialdom 'decried by Hamlet

parts.note: the To be or not to be soliloquy lists among life's ills the arrogance 'of office'

explanation.surface: Hamlet complains about the haughty manners of bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's soliloquy lists among life's burdens 'the insolence of office and the spurns that patient merit of the unworthy takes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemptuous rudeness is the quality Hamlet ascribes to men in office.

clue.text: .Judge to judge the rest, possibly

parts.note: to deem is to judge or consider

indicators.note: possibly means the following word could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A judge is asked to pass judgement on the remainder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges REST to STER after DEEM; 'the' is a link. A deemster is a judge on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A deemster is one of the two judges of the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Where Arkwright finished up

parts.note: not Richard Arkwright the inventor but the builder of the Ark, Noah, whose vessel came to rest on a mountain

explanation.surface: A question about where the industrialist Richard Arkwright ended his days.
explanation.walkthrough: Arkwright looks like the cotton-mill inventor, but an ark-wright builds an ark: Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says the Ark grounded on the mountains of Ararat in eastern Turkey.
